info.title: LoonFS HTTP API
info.description: Static OpenAPI document for the LoonFS v0 HTTP API.

get.description: Returns `ok` when the server is running and can accept requests.

Returns `ready` while the server admits new work. Once shutdown begins and publisher admission closes, answers 503 `shutting_down` so load balancers can drain the instance. `/health` stays the liveness probe: it only reports that the process is up.

503.description: Shutdown has begun; admission is closed

post.description: Creates or reuses a named, user-owned checkpoint record pinning the current namespace view. The record is a garbage-collection root until released or expired, so routine maintenance should flush the WAL instead. This is a maintenance/admin operation, not a file mutation.

400.description: Invalid namespace id, name, or lifetime

post.description: Releases a user-owned checkpoint pin by id. Idempotent: releasing an already-released or reaped record succeeds. The record is reaped by a later garbage-collection pass; its pinned data becomes collectable only on the pass after that.

400.description: Invalid id, or the checkpoint is fork-owned

post.description: Runs one mark-and-sweep garbage-collection pass under the format's safety rules (grace window, delete-time re-verification, retention wins). Nothing sweeps without this explicit call or a maintenance-tick opt-in.
Removes the namespace's index.grams feature entry and its segment references; garbage collection reclaims the segments. Idempotent.

200.description: Feature entry removed or already absent

503.description: Lost a manifest publication race; retry

post.description: Publishes the namespace's index.grams feature entry. Backfill over existing revisions starts on the next maintenance tick and the index stays current from then on. Idempotent.

200.description: Feature entry published or already present

503.description: Lost a manifest publication race; retry

post.description: Runs one bounded maintenance step: flushes the WAL tail once it reaches the threshold, and optionally runs a garbage-collection pass afterwards. Losing the root race is an outcome, not an error.
Advances the namespace retention floor after checkpoint state makes older WAL history unnecessary for normal replay.

Folds the visible WAL tail into metadata tables, publishes a manifest, and advances the metadata root to cover the current head. No checkpoint record is created; superseded manifests become garbage-collection candidates once nothing pins them. This is the routine latest-state maintenance operation.

200.description: Metadata root covers the current head

get.description: Returns a summary of supported features and limits.

409.description: Namespace already exists or is partial

410.description: Namespace id was deleted and retired

get.description: Returns the current head, manifest, checkpoint, WAL tail, and retention state for a namespace.

parameters.name: expected_head_seq
parameters.description: Delete only if the namespace head is still at this sequence

get.description: Returns committed changes from the write-ahead log. Callers can use this feed to keep another projection synchronized with WAL history.

parameters.name: after_seq
parameters.description: Return committed changes after this sequence

post.description: Applies an explicit semantic commit containing ordered inode-level operations and optional preconditions. Use this for advanced cases that require inode-specificity, preconditions, or batch transactions.

get.description: Returns file bytes for the current revision at a path, or for a specific retained revision when `revision_no` is provided.

404.description: Namespace, path, or revision not found

503.description: The server is at its concurrent content-read limit; retry shortly

get.description: Lists a directory at the current namespace head.

post.description: Runs one path-oriented filesystem mutation, such as create directory, put file, move, copy, delete, or restore revision. The commit id makes retries idempotent.

get.description: Resolves the current path to a file inode and returns revisions for that file. If the file could be renamed, use the inode revision API for stable identity.
Returns the current metadata for a path, including inode identity, kind, display name, and file content metadata.

post.description: Creates a new namespace as a fork from the source namespace's current durable view.

get.description: Returns revisions for a file inode, independent of the file's current path or later renames.
Returns bytes for one retained file revision by inode id and revision number.

404.description: Namespace, inode, or revision not found

503.description: The server is at its concurrent content-read limit; retry shortly

post.description: Appends a new current revision to a file inode using bytes from an older retained revision. The request includes the caller's expected current revision for race safety.

400.description: Invalid inode id, revision, or request

404.description: Namespace, inode, or revision not found

post.description: Searches file content with a regular expression, accelerated by the namespace's gram index (`index.grams`). Matches are verified against the real pattern and returned in ascending `(inode_id, byte_offset)` order; revisions committed after the index watermark are scanned exhaustively unless `allow_stale` skips them. Requires the index to be materialized on the namespace.

400.description: Invalid pattern, cursor, or an unindexable pattern without allow_scan

501.description: The gram index is not materialized on this namespace

503.description: The index trails the head past the scan budget

post.description: Starts an upload session for content that may later be attached to a file. Service-proxied uploads send bytes through the server; direct-put uploads return object-store presigned credentials.
Completes an upload session once the caller confirms the expected content reference. The response may include a short-lived validation token for a following file write.

put.description: Uploads bytes into a service-proxied upload session and returns the content reference for the stored object.

503.description: The server is at its concurrent proxied-upload limit; retry shortly

AdvanceRetentionResponse.description: Result of advancing the retention floor.

retention_floor_seq.description: New minimum sequence for incremental replay.

ApiError.description: HTTP error body used by LoonFS APIs.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable reason from the [`ErrorCode`](crate::ErrorCode)
registry.

Carried as a string so clients keep working when a newer server
introduces a code they do not know; use
[`ErrorCode::parse`](crate::ErrorCode::parse) for typed access.

oneOf.description:
Structured context for the code, present when the failure carries
machine-usable identity (API spec, "Standard error contract"). Boxed
so the rare detailed error does not widen every error-carrying result.

feature.description:
For `not_supported` errors, the capability-document feature key the
client should reconcile against.

request_id.description:
Correlation id the server assigned to the failed request; the same
value is sent as the `x-request-id` response header.

AuthoritativePathEntry.description:
Authoritative metadata for one visible path.

This is the result shape for stat/list style reads. File entries include
revision and content summary fields; directory entries leave those empty.

absolute_path.description: Absolute path as rendered from stored display names.

oneOf.description: Current content reference, for files.

display_name.description: Stored display name for this path component.

head_seq.description: Namespace head sequence this answer was read from.

inode_id.description: Stable inode identity for this item.

inode_kind.description: Whether the item is a file or directory.

oneOf.description: Parent directory inode, or `None` for the root.
Current file revision number, for files.

size_bytes.description: Current file size in bytes, for files.

BeginUploadRequest.description: Request for starting an upload session.

oneOf.description: Required for `direct_put`; the server signs exactly this content object.
Requested upload transport. Absent keeps the existing service-proxied path.

BeginUploadResponse.description: Response for starting an upload session.

CapabilityDocument.description:
A deployment's self-description (API spec, "Capability discovery").

A remote client fetches this from `GET /v0/config` and caches it; an
embedded engine exposes the same document as a constant. SDK gating logic
is therefore identical for both backends: check [`supports`] or
[`has_profile`], and treat a `not_supported` error as authoritative when
the two disagree.

[`supports`]: CapabilityDocument::supports
[`has_profile`]: CapabilityDocument::has_profile

features.description:
Named features and whether this deployment supports them. An absent
key means unsupported.

limits.description: Advisory numeric limits clients may use to pre-validate requests.

profiles.description:
Advertised profiles, each `plane/version`. All-or-nothing: every
required op of an advertised profile is implemented.

ChangeSeq.description:
Monotonically increasing namespace commit sequence number.

This is the global visibility order for a namespace.

CheckpointId.description:
Durable checkpoint identifier.

A checkpoint is a durable bookmark to a namespace manifest version.

CommitDelta.description:
Durable metadata fact exposed through the change feed.

Sync and projection clients can apply deltas directly.

CommitId.description:
Client-supplied idempotency key for one logical commit.

Reuse the same `CommitId` when retrying the same request.

oneOf.description: Create a directory under a parent inode.

oneOf.title: CommitOpCreateFile
oneOf.description: Create a file under a parent inode.

oneOf.title: CommitOpReplaceFile
oneOf.description: Append a new revision to an existing file.

oneOf.title: CommitOpRestoreRevision
oneOf.description: Restore a prior revision as a new current revision.

oneOf.title: CommitOpDeleteFile
oneOf.description: Delete a file inode.

oneOf.title: CommitOpRename
oneOf.description: Rename or move an inode.

oneOf.title: CommitOpDeleteSubtree
oneOf.description: Delete a directory subtree.

CommitOp.description: Semantic operation inside a commit request.

oneOf.title: CommitPreconditionInodeRevisionIs
oneOf.description: File inode is still at this revision.

oneOf.title: CommitPreconditionAncestorsNotSubtreeDeleted
oneOf.description: Inode ancestors have not been subtree-deleted.

oneOf.title: CommitPreconditionChildNameAbsent
oneOf.description: Directory child name is still absent.

oneOf.title: CommitPreconditionBindingIs
oneOf.description: Directory binding is still exactly the binding the caller saw.

oneOf.title: CommitPreconditionDirectoryEmpty
oneOf.description: Directory is still empty.

CommitPrecondition.description: Race check evaluated before a commit is accepted.

CommitRequest.description:
Explicit semantic commit request.

Use this lower-level shape when you need one commit id, optional
preconditions, and multiple ordered operations.

commit_id.description: Client idempotency key for this logical commit.

preconditions.description: Optional race checks evaluated before mutation.

CommitResponse.description:
Result of one committed mutation.

Every mutation resolves to this envelope — path-oriented operations and
explicit commits, embedded or remote. The commit id is the caller's
reconciliation handle: resubmitting the same request with the same id
replays this result instead of committing twice.

commit_id.description:
Idempotency key the mutation committed under: caller-supplied, or
generated on the caller's behalf when the request carried none.

committed_seq.description: Sequence number where the mutation became visible.

CommittedChange.description: One committed change in namespace order.

commit_id.description: Client idempotency key for this logical commit.

seq.description: Namespace sequence for this logical commit.

CompleteUploadRequest.description: Request to complete an upload with the expected content ref.

CompleteUploadResponse.description: Response after an upload session is completed.

ContentRef.description:
Pointer to immutable file content.

A `ContentRef` is safe to publish only after the referenced bytes are
durable in the namespace's content store.

kind.description: Content strategy used by the referenced object.

size_bytes.description: Complete byte length of the referenced file content.

ContentStoreId.description:
Durable id for an immutable content store.

Content stores own file bytes. Namespaces point at content stores.

CopyBehavior.description: Copy behavior for path-oriented copies, mirroring [`PutBehavior`].

CreateCheckpointRequest.description: Request to create a durable checkpoint pin.

name.description:
Label recorded on the checkpoint record. A label, not a key: several
records may carry the same name over different bases.

ttl_ms.description:
Optional lifetime; the server computes the record's expiry from its
own clock. Absent means the pin holds until explicitly released.

CreateCheckpointResponse.description: Result of creating or reusing a checkpoint.

oneOf.description: Manifest `metadata/root.json` references after the operation.

expires_at_ms.description: Expiry recorded on the record, when the request carried a `ttl_ms`.

DeleteDirectoryBehavior.description: Directory delete behavior for path-oriented deletes.

head_seq.description:
The head's last committed sequence; the delete linearized
immediately after it, so this is where history ended.

DirectPutUpload.description: Presigned direct_put upload details. The raw object key is intentionally not public.

DisableGramsIndexResponse.description: Result of disabling the gram index on a namespace (admin plane).

namespace_id.description: Namespace the feature entry was removed from.

was_enabled.description: False when the namespace had no feature entry to remove.

EnableGramsIndexResponse.description: Result of enabling the gram index on a namespace (admin plane).

already_enabled.description: True when the namespace already carried the feature entry.

built_through_seq.description:
Backfill covers commits at or below this sequence; later commits
arrive through WAL replay once backfill completes.

namespace_id.description: Namespace the feature entry was published for.

ErrorDetails.description:
Structured, machine-readable context accompanying an [`ApiError`].

Every field is optional: a code populates the fields that apply to it
(API spec, "Standard error contract"), and clients must tolerate absent
fields exactly as they tolerate unknown codes. Retry decisions still key
off the code; these fields carry the identity a caller needs to act —
which commit to resubmit, which epoch displaced it, which revision the
precondition saw.

active_writer.description:
Writer id recorded by the current epoch's acquirer, when the head
recorded one.

oneOf.description: Epoch that currently owns the namespace.
Revision that is actually current; absent when the inode has none.
Change-feed cursor the request asked to resume after.
Idempotency key of the mutation the error concerns.
Revision the request expected to be current.
Epoch the failing writer session held when it was displaced.
Inode the failed precondition or operation targeted.
Oldest sequence still promised for incremental replay.

committed_seq.description: Namespace sequence that created this revision.

inode_id.description: File inode that owns this revision.

revision_no.description: Revision number within the file inode.

oneOf.title: FsOpCreateDirectory
oneOf.description: Create one directory.

oneOf.title: FsOpPutFile
oneOf.description: Create or replace one file with an already-durable content ref.

oneOf.title: FsOpDeletePath
oneOf.description: Delete one path.

oneOf.title: FsOpMovePath
oneOf.description: Move one path to another path.

oneOf.title: FsOpCopyPath
oneOf.description: Copy one file path to another path.

oneOf.title: FsOpRestoreRevision
oneOf.description: Restore an older revision as the current revision for a path.

FilesystemOperationRequest.description: Request wrapper for one path-oriented operation.

commit_id.description: Caller-supplied idempotency key for this operation.

content_tokens.description: Proofs for any new external content refs introduced by this operation.

FlushWalOutcome.description: How one WAL flush satisfied its goal.

FlushWalResponse.description: Result of one WAL flush: how the metadata root covers the head.

namespace_id.description: Namespace whose WAL tail was flushed.

outcome.description: How the root came to cover the head.

target_head_seq.description: Head sequence the flush attempted to cover.

new_namespace_id.description: Durable namespace id for the fork target.

GcRequest.description:
Optional overrides for one garbage-collection pass. Absent fields use
the server's conservative defaults.

grace_window_ms.description:
Objects younger than this are never deleted, reachable or not. The
window has a derived safety floor (publication budgets plus provider
deadlines); a smaller value is rejected as `invalid_request`.

reap_window_ms.description:
Abandoned bootstrap trees older than this may be reaped. Must be at
least the grace window.

GcResponse.description: Result of one mark-and-sweep garbage-collection pass.

degraded_retention.description: True when ambiguous roots suppressed manifest/table deletion.

deleted_checkpoint_records.description: Released or expired checkpoint records deleted.

reaped_abandoned_objects.description: Objects removed while reaping an abandoned bootstrap tree.

released_fork_checkpoints.description:
Fork-owned checkpoint records released because their target namespace
is provably gone.

retained_candidates.description:
Candidates retained at delete time (grace window, missing
timestamps, or reachable from the fresh root set).

absolute_path.description: The file's absolute path, derived at the snapshot.

byte_offset.description: Byte offset of the match within the file.

inode_id.description: Durable identity of the matched file.

line.description: The matching line, truncated to the server's line cap.

line_number.description: One-based line number of the match.

revision_no.description: The matched revision (the newest visible one at the snapshot).

allow_scan.description:
Permit a capped exhaustive scan when the pattern yields no required
grams. Refused beyond the server's scan budget.

allow_stale.description:
When the unindexed tail exceeds the scan budget, return
indexed-only results (reported via `tail_scanned: false`) instead
of failing with `index_lagging`.

case_insensitive.description:
Match case-insensitively. Verification is exact; the index remains
consulted through its case-folded grams.

cursor.description:
Resume cursor from a previous page. The cursor resumes strictly
after the last candidate the issuing page finished scanning and is
bound to that page's request; each page is evaluated against the
namespace head at page time.

path_prefix.description: Restrict matches to files under this absolute path prefix.

pattern.description:
The pattern, in the Rust `regex` crate's dialect (no backreferences
or lookaround). Patterns that require no literal bytes are rejected
with `query_unindexable` unless `allow_scan` is set.

built_through_seq.description: Commits at or below this sequence were answered from the index.

head_seq.description:
Sequence this page was evaluated at. Pages are evaluated against
the namespace head at page time; the cursor is an ordering resume,
not a snapshot pin.

matches.description:
Matches in ascending `(inode_id, byte_offset)` order. A page may
return fewer matches than its limit and still carry a cursor: the
per-page verified-candidate budget bounds how much content one
request reads, whatever the plan's false-positive rate.

tail_scanned.description:
True when revisions after `built_through_seq` were scanned
exhaustively; false only when `allow_stale` skipped them.

InodeId.description:
Numeric identity of a file or directory within a namespace.

Inodes are stable across renames.

head_seq.description: Namespace head sequence used for the read.

inode_id.description: File inode whose revisions were returned.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, if more revisions are available.

ListPathEntriesResponse.description:
One directory listing and the namespace head it was answered at.

The envelope names the listing target and head so an empty directory
still tells the caller which state it observed, and so the response can
grow without reshaping `entries`.

absolute_path.description: Absolute path of the listed directory.

entries.description:
Directory entries for this page.

Entries are returned in canonical name-key order. Higher-level display
surfaces may sort entries separately for presentation.

head_seq.description: Namespace head sequence this listing was read from.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, if more entries remain.

oneOf.description: The WAL tail was below the threshold; the root was left alone.
The tick flushed the WAL tail and advanced the metadata root.

manifest_head_seq.description: Sequence covered by the published manifest.

oneOf.description:
The root already covered the attempted sequence — another publisher
got there first.

attempted_seq.description: Sequence this tick attempted to flush through.

oneOf.description: A concurrent head update won the race.

observed_head_seq.description: Head sequence observed before the advance attempt.

MaintenanceTickRequest.description:
Options for one explicit maintenance tick. Absent fields use the
server's defaults; garbage collection runs only when `gc` is present.

oneOf.description:
Run the mark-and-sweep garbage collector after the tick's
flush work. Nothing sweeps unless this is present.

max_wal_tail_segments.description:
Flush the visible WAL tail into metadata tables when it reaches this
many segments.

MaintenanceTickResponse.description: Result of one explicit maintenance tick.

oneOf.description: Garbage-collection report when the tick opted into sweeping.

status_before.description: Namespace status observed before the tick acted.

ManifestId.description:
Monotonically increasing namespace manifest identity.

This is the durable file-set version identity for namespace manifests.
Initial/fork manifests may be seeded from the current head sequence, but
later manifest ids can advance for checkpoint metadata, compaction, or
fork/index metadata without a new namespace commit.

MoveBehavior.description: Move behavior for path-oriented moves, mirroring [`PutBehavior`].

NameKey.description:
Name-policy-derived directory entry key.

Use this for exact name preconditions. Keep user-facing spelling in
`DisplayName`.

NamespaceId.description:
Durable id for one namespace.

A namespace is one filesystem history. This id is not a display name and
should not be reused after destruction.

NamespaceStatusResponse.description:
Status summary for one namespace.

This is the point-lookup answer to "does this namespace exist, and where
is its head?" — cheaper than listing all namespaces when only one matters.

oneOf.description: Current manifest pointer recorded by the head.

retention_floor_seq.description: Oldest sequence still promised for incremental replay.

wal_tail_segments.description: Number of visible WAL segments after the current manifest.

NamespaceSummary.description: Short namespace identifier returned by namespace create/fork operations.

oneOf.title: ObjectTransferAccessPresignedUrl
oneOf.description: Short-lived URL plus required headers for one object-store write.

headers.description: Headers that are covered by the signature and must be sent.

method.description: HTTP method the client must use.

PutBehavior.description: Put behavior for path-oriented file writes.

ReleaseCheckpointResponse.description: Result of releasing a checkpoint pin.

was_active.description:
True when this call flipped an active record to released; false when
the record was already released or no longer exists. Release is
idempotent — the end state is the same either way.

RestoreFileRevisionRequest.description: Request to restore a file revision by inode.

base_revision_no.description: Current revision the caller expects to replace.

RevisionNo.description: Monotonically increasing file revision counter within one file inode.

UploadContentResponse.description: Response after uploading bytes into a session.

UploadId.description: Durable id for one upload session.

ValidatedContentToken.description: Stateless proof that a LoonFS server already validated a content ref.

token.description: Opaque, server-signed token. Clients must not parse it.

WriterEpoch.description: Monotonically increasing writer epoch for namespace write fencing.
